clue.text: Re-organised to look impressive

definitions.note: a phrase where the answer is an adjective; read as 'impressive-looking'

indicators.note: the prefix re- asks for the following word to be put together again, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone reshuffles a display so that it looks more striking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Re-' makes 'organised' its own anagram fodder: reorganise the letters of ORGANISED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something grandiose is showy and pompous, made to look imposing.

clue.text: Concerned with a boy's motive

parts.note: re means concerning or about, as in business letters
a boy is a son

explanation.surface: Someone asks what drove a lad to do something.
explanation.definitionFit: A motive is the ground or cause for an action, the same as a reason.

clue.text: Edward's bearing up-river, as required

parts.note: N, north, is a compass bearing

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for the river is written bottom to top

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales
Ed is short for Edward; the 's means 'has'

explanation.surface: Edward is heading upstream as he was told to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' only makes sense in a down entry: the river is read from the bottom upwards. Edward's piece goes last although the clue names him first.
explanation.definitionFit: What is needed is what is required, both meaning necessary.

clue.text: What the climber aims for is a very cool head

definitions.text: What the climber aims for is a very cool head

parts.words: What the climber aims for is a very cool head
parts.note: a mountaineer heads for the summit, which on a high peak is capped with frozen water, a literally cold top

explanation.surface: A mountaineer's goal is to stay calm under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: The frozen covering of a summit or pole is literally an icy cap on top.

clue.text: Not naturally bright

parts.note: reads as 'a bit dim', but means getting no daylight from the sky

explanation.surface: Someone is described as not very clever by nature.
explanation.definitionFit: A place with no sunshine is not lit by nature's own light.

clue.text: A game swimmer encompasses it with some strain

indicators.note: the fish's name goes round the other two pieces, so it surrounds them

parts.note: a sole is a flatfish, so a swimmer
a strain is a tune, also called an air

explanation.surface: A sporty swimmer works hard through some exertion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strain' looks like effort; it is a musical strain.
explanation.definitionFit: Patience played alone with cards or pegs is the one-player pastime of that name.

clue.text: The group might see changes-there's nothing in that

indicators.note: the zero sign goes into the middle of the shuffled letters
the letters of 'might see' are altered into a new order

parts.note: O looks like the figure zero, meaning nothing

explanation.surface: A band might experience a lineup shake-up that has no effect.
explanation.walkthrough: MIGHT SEE rearranges to EIGHTSME, and O goes inside to make the eight-person set; an eightsome reel is a Scottish dance for eight.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of eight dancers or players forms a company of that size.

clue.text: Notices a fly going up and down

parts.note: to notice is to see, so notices gives sees
to wing is to fly

explanation.surface: Someone spots an insect bobbing about in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly' looks like the insect, but it is the verb, 'to wing'.
explanation.definitionFit: A see-saw moves alternately up and down, so this is the motion of one.

clue.text: A port in Alaska that's chang ingrapidly

definitions.meaning: a Gulf Coast harbour city, though in fact it is in Alabama
describes something moving or shifting easily, as a face full of expression

explanation.surface: A harbour town is described as being in constant flux.
explanation.walkthrough: The city of Mobile is really in Alabama, not Alaska; the clue as printed gets the state wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit one word: the Alabama port city, and an adjective for shifting or moving easily.

clue.text: Created a row about Oriental girl

parts.note: made means created

indicators.note: the line of things goes round the letter for east

parts.note: a row of things is a line
E, east, is the Orient

explanation.surface: Someone started an argument about an Eastern woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel; it is a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeleine is a female first name.

clue.text: " are a good handmaid, but the worst mistress'(Bacon)

definitions.text: are a good handmaid, but the worst mistress'(Bacon)

parts.words: are a good handmaid, but the worst mistress'(Bacon)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Francis Bacon's essays: the missing word is the subject of the saying, wealth that serves well but rules badly

explanation.surface: A line from Bacon about something that serves well but dominates badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacon's saying is about wealth: a fine servant when kept in its place, a tyrant when it takes control.

clue.text: Related to dreadful bore

definitions.note: the past tense of bear, to put up with

indicators.note: dreadful suggests the letters are in a terrible mess, so they are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone is kin to a tedious person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' looks like a dull person; it is the past tense of 'bear'.
explanation.definitionFit: If you bore something, you endured it or put up with it.

clue.text: A capital campaign maxim!

parts.note: a war is a military campaign
a saw is an old saying

explanation.surface: A slogan for a political drive in a big city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'campaign maxim' reads as a slogan; it is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The city in question is the seat of Poland's government.

clue.text: Well-known artist swindles the board

parts.note: a con is a swindle
a board is a table

explanation.surface: A famous painter cheats the company's directors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the board' sounds like directors; it is a table. John Constable was an English landscape painter.
explanation.definitionFit: John Constable is a celebrated English landscape painter.

clue.text: The little bird for which crumbled bread lay around

indicators.note: the word for lay is placed round the scrambled letters

parts.note: lay, the past of lie, is to have been at rest

indicators.note: bread that has crumbled is broken up, so its letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A small bird pecks at broken bread scattered about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumbled' and 'around' are the two indicators: the shuffled bread sits inside the word for lay. Robin redbreast is the British folk name for the robin.
explanation.definitionFit: The robin is commonly called by this name for its red-orange chest.

clue.text: State whereabouts

definitions.meaning: a state of affairs or condition

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a set of circumstances and a place where something is sited.

clue.text: A supplementary note backing a crawler

indicators.note: going backwards, so the letters for the note are written right to left

parts.note: PS, postscript, is a note added at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A footnote supports a sycophant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crawler' looks like a toady; it is a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: The asp is a snake, a creature that crawls along the ground.

clue.text: Some had a good reputation in the past

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are used, a run within them

explanation.surface: Some people used to have a fine name.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits in 'hAD A GOod'.
explanation.definitionFit: Long ago means earlier, at a time gone by.

clue.text: Copper turning to drug

parts.note: a copper is a penny coin, abbreviated P

indicators.note: turning round means the little word is written backwards

explanation.surface: A police officer becomes a narcotics user.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman; it is a penny, P, the old copper coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Pot is slang for cannabis.

clue.text: Making a start, though split

definitions.meaning: a gap or crack, as a noun

explanation.surface: Getting something under way even though it is cracked.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both beginning and a gap or aperture.

clue.text: He never sees where he's heading for

definitions.text: He never sees where he's heading for

parts.words: He never sees where he's heading for
parts.note: a rower sits facing backwards, so travels without looking at the destination

explanation.surface: A man is always heading somewhere blindly.
explanation.definitionFit: A rower faces the stern, so moves forward with his back to where the boat is going.

clue.text: Choose a casual sort of shirt after work

indicators.note: the shirt letter comes after the letters for work

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
a T-shirt is a casual shirt

explanation.surface: Picking something informal to wear after the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' looks like a job; it is an opus.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt is to choose or decide on.

clue.text: A company unreasonably circumscribed by design

indicators.note: enclosed by the word for design, so the excess word sits inside it

parts.note: a design is a plan
too means excessively, beyond what is reasonable

explanation.surface: A firm is overly constrained by a pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'company' looks like a business; it is a military unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A platoon is a small body of soldiers, a subdivision of an army company.

clue.text: Contribution expected? Keep calm!

parts.note: a sub, subscription, is a regular contribution
due means expected, as a train is due

explanation.surface: Asking someone to hold steady while a payment is awaited.
explanation.definitionFit: To subdue is to quieten or hold down, keeping a situation under control.

clue.text: Reporter playing a Shakespearean role

definitions.meaning: something that makes a report, a bang, as a gun does
Falstaff's swaggering crony in Henry V and the Henry IV plays

explanation.surface: A journalist acting a part in a Shakespeare play.
explanation.definitionFit: The handgun makes a report when fired, and Falstaff's companion in Shakespeare bears its name.

clue.text: Good man on telephone line

parts.note: ST, saint, is a good man
to ring is to telephone

explanation.surface: A virtuous man is using the phone line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'line' looks like a phone line; it is cord.
explanation.definitionFit: String is cord or thread, a length of line.

clue.text: Only heartless guys are pompous

parts.note: sole means only

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word for guys is taken out

parts.note: guys are men

explanation.surface: Unfeeling blokes are self-important.
explanation.definitionFit: Solemn here means stiffly formal and self-important.

clue.text: Spoiling in a tot, is a certain over-indulgence

indicators.note: spoiling suggests the order of the letters is ruined, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Indulging a child too much is a definite excess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoiling' looks like indulging a tot; it is the anagram signal for IN A TOT IS A.
explanation.definitionFit: Satiation is being filled beyond the point of desire, a kind of excess.

clue.text: When a gentleman is in the middle of paid party political workers

indicators.note: the gentleman word sits inside the word for when

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'
a gent is a gentleman

explanation.surface: A man sits among the people paid to campaign for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Political parties employ agents to organise campaigns in constituencies.

clue.text: The manager continued to go by water

parts.note: a river is a body of water

explanation.surface: The boss carried on travelling by boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go by' is a link joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A contriver manages or engineers things, someone who brings matters about.

clue.text: Property-owner giving minor gold

parts.note: less means smaller or minor
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A landlord hands out a little gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A lessor is the landlord who grants a lease.

clue.text: Rude in a gentle fashion

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Someone is impolite in a polite manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' looks like a manner; it is the anagram signal turning A GENTLE into ELEGANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude here means rough and unrefined, lacking grace.
